detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → MBBS / Doctor → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NEET UG. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study MBBS / Doctor
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5.5 Years. You will learn Anatomy and body systems, Diseases and medicines, Diagnosis and treatment, and Surgery and emergency care.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in MBBS / Doctor
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: NEET UG

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: NEET UG is required for the applicable medical admissions. The qualifying mark and the actual admission cutoff are different; the admission cutoff depends on college, year, category and seat type.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ
detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

cutoffGuidance: NEET UG rank/counselling determines admission; the closing rank changes every year by category, college, course and counselling round.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BDS / Dentist → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NEET UG. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BDS / Dentist
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5 Years. You will learn Teeth and mouth, Dental diseases, Dental procedures, and Patient care.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BDS / Dentist
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BHMS / Homeopathic Medicine → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NEET UG, NCHM JEE or college admission route, depending on institution. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BHMS / Homeopathic Medicine
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5.5 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Theory, Practical/project work, and Communication and job skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BHMS / Homeopathic Medicine
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: NEET UG is required for the applicable medical admissions. The qualifying mark and the actual admission cutoff are different; the admission cutoff depends on college, year, category and seat type.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NEET UG. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BSMS / Siddha Medicine
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5.5 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Theory, Practical/project work, and Communication and job skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BSMS / Siddha Medicine
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BVSc & Animal Husbandry → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NEET UG. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BVSc & Animal Husbandry
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5.5 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Theory, Practical/project work, and Communication and job skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BVSc & Animal Husbandry
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → GNM Nursing → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study GNM Nursing
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3 Years. You will learn Human body and health, Patient care, Medicines and nursing procedures, and Hospital practice.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in GNM Nursing
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → B.Pharm → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Pharm
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Medicines and how they work, Pharmacy practice, Drug safety, and Dispensing and patient guidance.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Pharm
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → BPT Physiotherapy → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study BPT Physiotherapy
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4.5 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Theory, Practical/project work, and Communication and job skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BPT Physiotherapy
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Radiology & Imaging Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Radiology & Imaging Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Radiology & Imaging Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Anesthesia Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Anesthesia Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Anesthesia Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Cardiac Care Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Nutrition & Dietetics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Nutrition & Dietetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Nutrition & Dietetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Emergency Medical Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Emergency Medical Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Emergency Medical Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Dialysis Therapy → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Dialysis Therapy
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Dialysis Therapy
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Perfusion Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take PCB / Science subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Perfusion Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Perfusion Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Health Information Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Health Information Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Public Health → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take 12th / course-specific eligibility subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Public Health
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Public Health
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Forensic Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Forensic Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Forensic Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Genetics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Genetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Genetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Microbiology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take 12th / course-specific eligibility subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Microbiology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Microbiology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience
