detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Clinical Research → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take 12th / course-specific eligibility subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Clinical Research
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Clinical Research
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Computer Science Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Computer Science Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Computer Science Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Data Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Data Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Data Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Information Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Information Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Information Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Electronics & Communication → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Electronics & Communication
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Electronics & Communication
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: JEE Main

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: JEE Main eligibility/qualifying rules and college closing ranks are different things. The final rank needed changes by college, branch, year, category and counselling.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

cutoffGuidance: JEE Main has a national percentile/rank system; KCET/COMEDK and college cutoffs are separate. Closing ranks change every year by college, branch, category and quota.

babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Electrical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Electrical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Mechanical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Civil Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Civil Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Civil Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Aeronautical Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Aeronautical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Aeronautical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Chemical Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Chemical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Chemical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ

cutoffGuidance: JEE Main has a national percentile/rank system; KCET/COMEDK and college cutoffs are separate. Closing ranks change every year by college, branch, category and quota.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Biomedical Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take 12th / course-specific eligibility subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Biomedical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Biomedical Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: JEE Main eligibility/qualifying rules and college closing ranks are different things. The final rank needed changes by college, branch, year, category and counselling.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Robotics Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Robotics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Robotics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Mechatronics Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Mechatronics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Mechatronics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Petroleum Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Petroleum Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Petroleum Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: JEE Main

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: JEE Main eligibility/qualifying rules and college closing ranks are different things. The final rank needed changes by college, branch, year, category and counselling.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ
detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

cutoffGuidance: JEE Main has a national percentile/rank system; KCET/COMEDK and college cutoffs are separate. Closing ranks change every year by college, branch, category and quota.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Mining Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Mining Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Food Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Food Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Food Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Instrumentation Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Instrumentation Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Instrumentation Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Production Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Production Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Production Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ

cutoffGuidance: JEE Main has a national percentile/rank system; KCET/COMEDK and college cutoffs are separate. Closing ranks change every year by college, branch, category and quota.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Marine Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Marine Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Marine Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: JEE Main

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: JEE Main eligibility/qualifying rules and college closing ranks are different things. The final rank needed changes by college, branch, year, category and counselling.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Renewable Energy Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Renewable Energy Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Renewable Energy Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Internet of Things → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Internet of Things
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Internet of Things
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Software Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Software Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Software Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: JEE Main

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: JEE Main eligibility/qualifying rules and college closing ranks are different things. The final rank needed changes by college, branch, year, category and counselling.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ
detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

cutoffGuidance: JEE Main has a national percentile/rank system; KCET/COMEDK and college cutoffs are separate. Closing ranks change every year by college, branch, category and quota.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects

babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Blockchain Technology

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
