detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech VLSI Design → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech VLSI Design
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech VLSI Design
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Geoinformatics Engineering → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Geoinformatics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Geoinformatics Engineering
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Tech Construction Technology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete JEE Main, State/University engineering entrance where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Tech Construction Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core engineering concepts, Mathematics and problem-solving, Tools/software/equipment used in the field, and Projects and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Tech Construction Technology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Physics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Physics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Physics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Mathematics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Mathematics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Mathematics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Statistics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Statistics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Statistics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Data Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Data Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Data Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Artificial Intelligence → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Artificial Intelligence
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Artificial Intelligence
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Environmental Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Environmental Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Environmental Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Geophysics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Geophysics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Geophysics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Astronomy & Astrophysics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Astronomy & Astrophysics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Astronomy & Astrophysics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Zoology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Zoology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Zoology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Botany
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs

babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Botany
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Genetics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Genetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Genetics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Food Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Food Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Food Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Forensic Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Forensic Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Forensic Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Climate Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Climate Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Climate Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Nanotechnology → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Nanotechnology
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Nanotechnology
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Actuarial Science → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Science / PCM or PCB depending on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Actuarial Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Actuarial Science
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Com Accounting & Finance → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Commerce / any accepted stream subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Com Accounting & Finance
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Business basics, Accounting/finance/management concepts, Real-world business cases, and Projects and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Com Accounting & Finance
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Com Banking & Insurance → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Commerce / any accepted stream subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Com Banking & Insurance
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Business basics, Accounting/finance/management concepts, Real-world business cases, and Projects and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Com Banking & Insurance
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Com International Business → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Commerce / any accepted stream subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Com International Business
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Business basics, Accounting/finance/management concepts, Real-world business cases, and Projects and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Com International Business
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.
