topRecruiters: Leading employers, government organizations, multinational companies, startups and sector-specific organizations
topRecruitersKn: ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಉದ್ಯೋಗದಾತರು, ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳು, ಬಹುರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಕಂಪನಿಗಳು, ಸ್ಟಾರ್ಟ್‌ಅಪ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ-ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳು

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA Foreign Languages → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA Foreign Languages
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA Foreign Languages
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.studentNote: Baby-step rule: the exact entrance exam, Class 12 subjects, minimum marks, internship and licence requirements can differ by college/state/professional regulator. Always check the latest official admission notice before applying.

detailedPathwayKn.simpleSummary: 10/12ನೇ ತರಗತಿ → ಅಗತ್ಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ/ಮೆರಿಟ್ → ಕಾಲೇಜು ಪ್ರವೇಶ → ಕೋರ್ಸ್ → ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ತರಬೇತಿ → ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಅಥವಾ ಉನ್ನತ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ
detailedPathwayKn.note: ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್, ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲೇಜಿನ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿವರ್ಷ ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಹಾಕುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

cutoffGuidance: CUET/university merit cutoffs vary by institution, subject combination and category.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.

babySteps.title: Study BA Film Studies
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA Fine Arts → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete College/university entrance or portfolio test, where applicable. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA Fine Arts
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA Fine Arts
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: College/university entrance or portfolio test, where applicable

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA Dance → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA Dance
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA Dance
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA Social Work → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA Social Work
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA Social Work
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA Gender Studies → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA Gender Studies
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Reading and theory, Projects/fieldwork, and Communication and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA Gender Studies
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BA LLB → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BA LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5 Years. You will learn Constitution and laws, Legal reasoning, Case studies, and Legal writing and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BA LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → BBA LLB → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Commerce / any accepted stream subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BBA LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5 Years. You will learn Business basics, Accounting/finance/management concepts, Real-world business cases, and Projects and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BBA LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc LLB → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 5 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3 Years. You will learn Constitution and laws, Legal reasoning, Case studies, and Legal writing and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in LLB
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → Corporate Law → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study Corporate Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3-5 Years. You will learn Constitution and laws, Legal reasoning, Case studies, and Legal writing and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Corporate Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → Intellectual Property Law → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study Intellectual Property Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3-5 Years. You will learn Constitution and laws, Legal reasoning, Case studies, and Legal writing and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Intellectual Property Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → International Law → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Any stream (course-specific subjects may apply) subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CLAT / university law entrance, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study International Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3-5 Years. You will learn Constitution and laws, Legal reasoning, Case studies, and Legal writing and practical work.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in International Law
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Aviation → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Aviation
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Aviation
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

exams.name: CUET UG / university admission, depending on college

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study BBA Aviation Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Business basics, Accounting/finance/management concepts, Real-world business cases, and Projects and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in BBA Aviation Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → B.Sc Aeronautics → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take 12th / course-specific eligibility subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete CUET UG / university admission, depending on college. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study B.Sc Aeronautics
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects of the field, Theory and concepts, Laboratory/project work where applicable, and Problem-solving and practical skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in B.Sc Aeronautics
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → Airport Management → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study Airport Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Industry basics, Safety and service skills, Hands-on training, and Customer and workplace skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Airport Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → Air Traffic Management → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study Air Traffic Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Core subjects, Theory, Practical/project work, and Communication and job skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Air Traffic Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → entrance exam → admission → Hotel Management / BHM → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Take the required entrance exam
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare for and complete NCHM JEE or college admission route, depending on institution. Some colleges may admit students without this exam.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your entrance score/rank may be used to decide admission.

babySteps.title: Apply for colleges
babySteps.whatToDo: Fill the college/university application or counselling form, enter your choices, and submit the required documents.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This is how you compete for a seat in the course.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check your rank/merit, cutoff and seat allotment. If selected, accept the seat and complete document verification and fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially become a student of the course.

babySteps.title: Study Hotel Management / BHM
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Industry basics, Safety and service skills, Hands-on training, and Customer and workplace skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Hotel Management / BHM
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → Event Management → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study Event Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 3 Years. You will learn Industry basics, Safety and service skills, Hands-on training, and Customer and workplace skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Event Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → Hospitality Management → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study Hospitality Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about Usually 3-4 Years. You will learn Industry basics, Safety and service skills, Hands-on training, and Customer and workplace skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Hospitality Management
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
entranceAndAdmission.cutoffInfo: There is no one fixed cutoff for every college. The required score/rank changes by year, college, course, category and seat type. For a real application, check the latest official counselling/college notice.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

nextSteps: Pass all required subjects and complete the qualification
Complete any compulsory internship/licence/registration/professional exam where applicable
Apply for entry-level jobs and build experience

detailedPathway.simpleSummary: Class 10 → Class 11-12 → admission → Cruise Ship Hospitality → practical training where required → pass the course → required licence/certification where applicable → job → career.

babySteps.title: Finish Class 10
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass Class 10 and choose the subjects you need for the next stage.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This gives you the school qualification needed to continue.

babySteps.title: Choose Class 11-12 subjects
babySteps.whatToDo: Take Usually 12th / stream depends on course subjects if required for this course. Check the college's current eligibility rules.
babySteps.whyItMatters: The subjects you study in Class 11-12 can decide which courses you are allowed to apply for.

babySteps.title: Pass Class 12
babySteps.whatToDo: Complete Class 12 and meet the minimum marks/subject requirements of the colleges you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You normally need to finish Class 12 before starting a bachelor's course.

babySteps.title: Apply for admission
babySteps.whatToDo: Apply to colleges/universities offering this course. Admission may be based on marks, merit, a university test, portfolio, or another college-specific process.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Different colleges use different admission methods.

babySteps.title: Get your seat
babySteps.whatToDo: Check the merit list/selection result. If selected, accept the seat, verify documents and pay the required fees.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you officially join the course.

babySteps.title: Study Cruise Ship Hospitality
babySteps.whatToDo: Join the course and study it for about 6-18 Months. You will learn Industry basics, Safety and service skills, Hands-on training, and Customer and workplace skills.
babySteps.whyItMatters: These are the main skills and knowledge you need for the field.

babySteps.title: Complete practical training / internship
babySteps.whatToDo: Attend the required labs, clinical practice, industrial training, internship or supervised work. The exact requirement depends on the course and college.
babySteps.whyItMatters: You learn how the job is actually done, not just from books.

babySteps.title: Pass and complete the course
babySteps.whatToDo: Pass your semesters/exams, complete projects or practical requirements, and receive your degree/diploma or professional qualification.
babySteps.whyItMatters: This proves that you completed the education needed for the next step.

babySteps.title: Get the required licence/certification, if any
babySteps.whatToDo: If this career has a compulsory registration, licence, internship completion or professional exam, finish that requirement before practising independently.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Some careers legally require an additional approval before you can work in that role.

babySteps.title: Apply for jobs
babySteps.whatToDo: Prepare your resume, apply to relevant employers, attend interviews and use your projects/internship experience to show what you can do.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Now you can start your professional career.

babySteps.title: Start your career in Cruise Ship Hospitality
babySteps.whatToDo: Start with an entry-level role related to the course, then build experience and take higher studies or specialisation if you want.
babySteps.whyItMatters: Your first job is the beginning of your long-term career path.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.

collegeStage.practicalTraining: Practical classes, labs, projects, fieldwork or supervised training are included where the course requires them. Internship/clinical training is compulsory only where the course or institution specifies it.

entranceAndAdmission.admissionProcess: Check eligibility → apply for the required exam/college → write the exam if required → check result/rank → check cutoff/merit → counselling or college choice filling → seat allotment → document verification → pay fees → join college.
